A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same OpenVLA generalization study. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable matching, including the later version's additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original algorithm comparisons, PPO ablations, generalization experiments and trajectory analyses in Figures 3–12 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds real-robot trials, action-chunking evaluations and articulated-object opening experiments in Appendices B.4–B.6.

M1.justification: The central shared-backbone PPO recipe remains unchanged. Appendix B.5 adds an adaptation for OpenVLA-OFT: four-action outputs, cumulative rewards over four steps and action-dimension-wise PPO clipping. This changes the procedure for the added variant, beyond simply evaluating another architecture.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates simulated pick-and-place tasks. v3 adds physical Franka Panda evaluation with six new objects and an articulated-object opening task with eight training objects, four unseen objects and six OOD conditions. These substantially broaden deployment environments and manipulation requirements.

E2.justification: A central comparator is substantially revised: process-supervised GRPO becomes outcome-supervised GRPO. Figure 3 removes the separate GRPO(s) comparison, while v1 Figure 10's additional GRPO variants disappear. Common-initial-state sampling survives within the revised GRPO, so this is more than renaming. PPO, PPO-ORZ and DPO/TPO comparisons remain.

E3.justification: GRPO changes from whole-parallel-batch grouping to 32 groups of eight trajectories, with successful episodes truncated and rewards assigned at termination. Added protocols include 30 matched-initial-condition physical trials, chunking experiments initialized with 400 unfiltered demonstrations and modified PPO settings, and door-opening evaluation using a 20-degree success threshold.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of whether the conclusions survive action chunking, distribution shifts in articulated-object manipulation and physical deployment, including qualitative analysis of real-robot failures. It removes the GRPO implementation sensitivity comparison in v1 Figure 10. Existing critic, warm-up, epoch, temperature and LoRA-rank ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report two-seed algorithm/design experiments and three-seed generalization results with standard deviations. The new tables extend existing mean/standard-deviation reporting; no changed uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased repeat count is stated for retained experiments.

E6.justification: The original OOD means and standard deviations are unchanged after table consolidation. Figure 3 replaces the GRPO results under its revised protocol, now showing learning. New Tables 2–4 report additional outcomes, including real-robot placement success of 0.27 for RL versus 0.00 for SFT, and chunked multi-receptacle success of 0.297 versus 0.365. These are new settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the future-sum, step-reward GRPO advantage definitions in v1 Equations 3–6 with a normalized trajectory-outcome advantage in v3 Equations 3–4. This is a substantive mathematical definition change. The POMDP formulation and SFT, PPO and DPO mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: a generalization benchmark, PPO's preference over GRPO/DPO, an efficient PPO recipe, and stronger semantic/execution generalization with comparable visual robustness. The added experiments do not revise these main claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 adds an explanation of physical-robot behavior: SFT overshoots, while RL iteratively corrects its pose despite jitter. B.5–B.6 interpret the additional results as extending applicability across architectures and tasks. The main limitations remain unchanged and now incorrectly describe all evaluation as simulated pick-and-place.

D1.justification: v3 supplies technical information for the extensions, including the OFT initialization checkpoint, unfiltered warm-up data, clipping ratio 0.1, discount factor 0.96 and GAE parameter 0.85. It also documents Panda/camera configurations and articulation reward and perturbation settings. The original implementation and project-access information largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists and related-work positioning are unchanged. The additional OpenVLA-OFT evaluation reuses the already cited Kim et al. (2025) work without redefining the paper's novelty claims.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the GRPO description, new Appendices B.4–B.6, acknowledgements, affiliations and conference header. The main narrative, section order, related work and conclusion are otherwise essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 consolidates the three original OOD tables into Table 1 and adds Tables 2–4 and Figures 12–14 for the new evaluations. It removes v1 Figure 10 and revises Figure 3's legend and vertical-axis range. These substantially change the supplementary displays, while the other original main-text figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendices B.4–B.6 substantially strengthen the empirical foundation by testing dependence on architecture, manipulation skill and simulated deployment—important restrictions of v1. PPO also remains ahead after GRPO is reworked into a learning comparator. The physical evaluation is preliminary at 30 trials, and mixed semantic findings and outdated limitations need better integration, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gain in evidence about the conclusions' applicability.
